parameters.sqlQuery:
-- Frontline MANAGER roster, scoped to workgroup 12056 (Frontline org root).
-- See the DEPTH LIMIT note in the scope block: only three hierarchy levels are
-- available in this table, so branches deeper than that are not matched.
--
-- Frontline MANAGER roster. Read the README sticky note: this table can no
-- longer produce an agent-level roster, only ~39 Frontline managers.
--
-- EVIDENCE (first successful run, snapshot 2026-09-10):
--   * emid is NULL across all 128,694 'Day' rows
--   * of 20,599 active Frontline rows only 39 carry any usable identity value
--   * employee, name, mgremid, manager and site all came back empty
--   * the surviving hierarchy columns are SHIFTED ONE LEVEL. On the sample row
--     emailaddress = kortega@wayfair.com while manager2 = 'Ortega, Karla' - the
--     row's own person - and srmanager = 'Worden, Emily' with
--     mgremailaddress = eworden@wayfair.com, that person's actual manager.
--
-- So this query reads mgr2emid/manager2 as the SUBJECT and
-- srmgremid/srmanager/mgremailaddress as the subject's MANAGER.
--
-- IF THAT IS BACKWARDS for other rows, swap the two marked blocks below. The
-- inference rests on one verified row plus the email match, so check a handful
-- of names in the sheet against the org chart before trusting it broadly.
--
-- Columns proven empty are REMOVED, not written blank: Office Location (site),
-- and the former Manager's Employee ID / Manager's Name (mgremid, manager).
--
-- Every value is COALESCEd to '' so blanks render as empty cells, not [null].

WITH latest_snapshot AS (
  SELECT MAX(date) AS snapshot_date
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager`
  WHERE datetype = 'Day'
    AND date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix'), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
                 AND CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix')
),
base AS (
  SELECT
    t.*,
    s.snapshot_date,
    -- Subject identity: numeric id first, then email, then login, then name
    COALESCE(
      NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(t.mgr2emid AS STRING)), ''),
      NULLIF(LOWER(TRIM(CAST(t.emailaddress AS STRING))), ''),
      NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(t.username AS STRING)), ''),
      NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(t.manager2 AS STRING)), '')
    ) AS employee_key
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager` AS t
  CROSS JOIN latest_snapshot AS s
  WHERE t.datetype = 'Day'
    AND t.date = s.snapshot_date
    AND t.stillatwayfair IS TRUE
    -- >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> FRONTLINE SCOPE - WORKGROUP 12056 <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<
    -- Scoped by workgroup id, the Frontline org root. Change the number in all
    -- three lines below to rescope.
    --
    -- DEPTH LIMIT - this matters. This table denormalizes only THREE hierarchy
    -- levels (wgid, parentwgid, grandparentwgid), so 12056 is only matchable
    -- when it sits at most two levels above the employee's workgroup. Per the
    -- Org Browser exports that covers e.g.
    --   12056 -> US Frontline (16409) -> Service Team 6 (16867)   REACHED
    -- but NOT deeper branches such as
    --   12056 -> B2B and Canada (16358) -> Multiple Contacts (17384)
    --         -> Multiple Contact Team 1 (3933)                   MISSED
    -- If the row count looks short, that is why. The zero-row diagnostic prints
    -- the full three-level hierarchy with ids so you can see where 12056 lands.
    --
    -- SAFE_CAST makes this type-agnostic; this table's column types do not
    -- match its schema documentation.
    --
    -- Previous scope, kept for reference - swap back by commenting the block
    -- below and uncommenting this line:
    --   AND t.team IN ('Frontline')
    -- Other verified team literals: 'Frontline Training', 'CARE', 'CAT',
    --   'Customer Service Outreach', 'Service Security Team'
    AND 12056 IN (
      SAFE_CAST(t.wgid AS INT64),
      SAFE_CAST(t.parentwgid AS INT64),
      SAFE_CAST(t.grandparentwgid AS INT64)
    )
    -- >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> END SCOPE <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<
)
SELECT
  -- >>> SUBJECT BLOCK - swap with the MANAGER BLOCK if the levels are reversed
  COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(b.mgr2emid AS STRING)), ''), '')  AS `Employee ID`,
  -- Single Full Name in "First Last" order. The source stores "Last, First",
  -- so the regex swaps the halves. A name with no comma passes through
  -- unchanged, because REGEXP_REPLACE returns its input when nothing matches.
  -- Sourced through a COALESCE so it works whichever name column is populated:
  -- manager2 holds the subject on this table, with employee and name as
  -- fallbacks in case either is ever backfilled.
  COALESCE(
    TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(
      COALESCE(
        NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(b.manager2 AS STRING)), ''),
        NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(b.employee AS STRING)), ''),
        NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(b.name AS STRING)), '')
      ),
      r'^([^,]+),\s*(.+)$', r'\2 \1'
    )),
    ''
  )                                                           AS `Full Name`,
  -- <<< END SUBJECT BLOCK
  COALESCE(LOWER(TRIM(CAST(b.emailaddress AS STRING))), '')   AS `Email Address`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(b.username AS STRING)), '')              AS `Sam Account Name`,
  IFNULL(FORMAT_DATE('%m/%d/%Y', SAFE_CAST(b.hiredate AS DATE)), '') AS `Start Date`,
  COALESCE(CAST(b.hierarchylevel AS STRING), '')              AS `Level`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(b.team AS STRING)), '')                  AS `Team`,
  COALESCE(CAST(b.wgid AS STRING), '')                        AS `Work Group ID`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(b.workgroup AS STRING)), '')             AS `Work Group`,
  COALESCE(CAST(b.parentwgid AS STRING), '')                  AS `Parent Work Group ID`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(b.parentworkgroup AS STRING)), '')       AS `Parent Work Group`,
  COALESCE(CAST(b.grandparentwgid AS STRING), '')             AS `Grandparent Work Group ID`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(b.grandparentparentworkgroup AS STRING)), '') AS `Grandparent Work Group`,
  -- >>> MANAGER BLOCK - swap with the SUBJECT BLOCK if the levels are reversed
  COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(CAST(b.srmgremid AS STRING)), ''), '') AS `Manager's Employee ID`,
  -- Same "First Last" convention as Full Name above
  COALESCE(
    TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(CAST(b.srmanager AS STRING)),
      r'^([^,]+),\s*(.+)$', r'\2 \1')),
    ''
  )                                                           AS `Manager's Name`,
  COALESCE(LOWER(TRIM(CAST(b.mgremailaddress AS STRING))), '') AS `Manager's Email`,
  -- <<< END MANAGER BLOCK
  COALESCE(CAST(b.snapshot_date AS STRING), '')               AS `Snapshot Date`
FROM base AS b
WHERE b.employee_key IS NOT NULL
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY b.employee_key ORDER BY b.lastrundate DESC) = 1
ORDER BY `Manager's Name`, `Full Name`

-- Runs ONLY when the roster query returns zero rows.
-- Prints the three-level workgroup hierarchy WITH IDS for the newest active
-- 'Day' snapshot, so you can see whether 12056 appears and at which level.
WITH latest_snapshot AS (
  SELECT MAX(date) AS snapshot_date
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager`
  WHERE datetype = 'Day'
    AND date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix'), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(CAST(t.grandparentwgid AS STRING), '(null)')                  AS gp_id,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(t.grandparentparentworkgroup AS STRING)), '(null)') AS gp_name,
  COALESCE(CAST(t.parentwgid AS STRING), '(null)')                       AS p_id,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(t.parentworkgroup AS STRING)), '(null)')            AS p_name,
  COALESCE(CAST(t.wgid AS STRING), '(null)')                             AS wg_id,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(t.workgroup AS STRING)), '(null)')                  AS wg_name,
  COUNT(*)                                                               AS row_count
FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager` AS t
CROSS JOIN latest_snapshot AS s
WHERE t.datetype = 'Day'
  AND t.date = s.snapshot_date
  AND t.stillatwayfair IS TRUE
GROUP BY gp_id, gp_name, p_id, p_name, wg_id, wg_name
ORDER BY row_count DESC
LIMIT 80

parameters.content:
## Frontline MANAGER Roster - Weekly Monday 4AM Arizona

### READ FIRST: this is managers, not agents
The original goal was agents as well as managers. This source cannot deliver that. Proven by the first successful run against snapshot 2026-09-10:

  * emid is NULL across all 128,694 'Day' rows
  * of 20,599 active Frontline rows, only 39 carry any usable identity value
  * employee, name, mgremid, manager and site are all empty

So the output is roughly 39 Frontline managers. Getting agents needs a different source - see NEXT STEPS.

### Names: one Full Name column, "First Last"
The separate Preferred First Name and Preferred Last Name columns are gone. A single Full Name column renders "First Last".

The source stores names as "Last, First", so the value is passed through REGEXP_REPLACE to swap the halves. A name with no comma passes through unchanged. The name is read through COALESCE(manager2, employee, name) so it resolves whichever column is populated - manager2 is the one carrying the subject on this table, with the other two as fallbacks if they are ever backfilled.

Manager's Name uses the same "First Last" convention so the sheet is internally consistent. To restore the source's native "Last, First" for either column, delete its REGEXP_REPLACE wrapper.

### The hierarchy columns are shifted one level
On the verified sample row, emailaddress = kortega@wayfair.com while manager2 = 'Ortega, Karla' - the row's OWN person - and srmanager = 'Worden, Emily' with mgremailaddress = eworden@wayfair.com, that person's manager.

The query therefore reads mgr2emid/manager2 as the SUBJECT and srmgremid/srmanager/mgremailaddress as the MANAGER. The SQL has these as two clearly marked blocks: SUBJECT BLOCK and MANAGER BLOCK. If the levels turn out reversed on other rows, swap the two blocks.

This inference rests on one row plus the email match. Spot-check a handful of names in the sheet against the org chart before relying on it.

### Columns removed because the source is empty
Office Location (site), Manager's Employee ID from mgremid, Manager's Name from manager. Earlier removals stand: everything that only exists in csn_hr.

All values are COALESCEd to '' so empty cells render blank rather than [null].

### 17 columns written
Employee ID, Full Name, Email Address, Sam Account Name, Start Date, Level, Team, Work Group ID, Work Group, Parent Work Group ID, Parent Work Group, Grandparent Work Group ID, Grandparent Work Group, Manager's Employee ID, Manager's Name, Manager's Email, Snapshot Date.

This workflow REPLACES row 1 of the tab.

### Scope: workgroup 12056 - READ THE DEPTH LIMIT
Scoped to workgroup 12056, the Frontline org root, matched at wgid, parentwgid or grandparentwgid.

DEPTH LIMIT: this table denormalizes only THREE hierarchy levels, so 12056 is matchable only when it sits at most two levels above an employee's workgroup. Per the Org Browser exports that reaches
  12056 -> US Frontline (16409) -> Service Team 6 (16867)      REACHED
but not deeper branches such as
  12056 -> B2B and Canada (16358) -> Multiple Contacts (17384) -> MC Team 1 (3933)   MISSED
Multiple Contacts teams in particular may be absent. Compare the row count against the team-based scope before trusting it.

Parent Work Group ID, Grandparent Work Group ID and Grandparent Work Group are now output columns so the hierarchy is visible in the sheet.

If it returns zero rows the diagnostic prints the whole three-level hierarchy with ids, marks any row containing 12056, and says whether 12056 is reachable at all.

FALLBACK, verified: AND t.team IN ('Frontline') returns 52,282 'Day' rows, 20,599 active, 1 day stale as of 2026-09-11. It is kept as a commented line in the scope block. Sibling teams: 'Frontline Training', 'CARE', 'CAT', 'Customer Service Outreach', 'Service Security Team'.

### Schedule
Workflow timezone America/Phoenix, cron 0 4 * * 1. Arizona skips DST so this is 11:00 UTC year-round. Confirm the timezone in Workflow Settings after import.

### Safety
Zero rows means the sheet is NOT cleared and the run fails with a per-column non-NULL profile naming the dead columns. A bad filter can never blank the sheet. The 30-day snapshot window is deliberately narrow so stale data is never published as current.

### NEXT STEPS for agent-level data
Two candidates, both needing an access check first:
  1. wf-gcp-us-ae-gat-prod.ops_reporting_layer.vw_customer_service_master_reporting
     Same project as the billing project already in use, so most likely to be
     reachable. Documented columns include employee_id, employee_name,
     employee_workgroup_id, employee_workgroup_name, employee_working_team,
     employee_working_site, employee_tenure, employee_login_username,
     employee_is_in_customer_service_org_flag.
  2. wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_datawarehouse.vw_dim_employee_detail

Run this to check reachability and grain, then the query can be repointed:
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows, COUNT(DISTINCT employee_id) AS employees
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-gat-prod.ops_reporting_layer.vw_customer_service_master_reporting`
  WHERE DATE(employee_date) >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
